paper_title: Enhancement of the Power-Conversion Efficiency of Organic Solar Cells via Unveiling an Appropriate Rational Design Strategy in Indacenodithiophene-alt-quinoxaline π-Conjugated Polymers

qa_pairs.question: What are the three structural optimization strategies investigated for enhancing the performance of indacenodithiophene-alt-quinoxaline (IDT-quinoxaline) polymers?
qa_pairs.answer: The study investigated three strategies: (1) increasing the number-average molecular weight (Mn) of the polymer, (2) replacing phenyl aryl substituents with thienyl groups on the indacenodithiophene (IDT) unit, and (3) enlarging the polymer backbone by replacing the IDT unit with indacenodithienothiophene (IDTT).
qa_pairs.source_title: Enhancement of the Power-Conversion Efficiency of Organic Solar Cells via Unveiling an Appropriate Rational Design Strategy in Indacenodithiophene-alt-quinoxaline π-Conjugated Polymers

qa_pairs.question: What is the maximum power conversion efficiency (PCE) achieved by a solar cell based on the ThIDT-TQxT polymer, and which acceptor was used?
qa_pairs.answer: A single-junction organic solar cell using the thienyl-substituted polymer ThIDT-TQxT blended with the acceptor PC71BM achieved a maximum power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 7.26%.
qa_pairs.source_title: Enhancement of the Power-Conversion Efficiency of Organic Solar Cells via Unveiling an Appropriate Rational Design Strategy in Indacenodithiophene-alt-quinoxaline π-Conjugated Polymers

qa_pairs.question: How does the substitution of phenyl rings with thienyl rings on the IDT unit affect the LUMO energy level of the resulting polymers?
qa_pairs.answer: Replacing phenyl substituents with thienyl groups results in a deeper LUMO level. For instance, ThIDT-TQxT has a LUMO of -3.66 eV compared to -3.56 eV for PhIDT-TQxT. This deepening is attributed to the sigma inductive effect of the thienyl rings.
qa_pairs.source_title: Enhancement of the Power-Conversion Efficiency of Organic Solar Cells via Unveiling an Appropriate Rational Design Strategy in Indacenodithiophene-alt-quinoxaline π-Conjugated Polymers

qa_pairs.question: Based on GIWAXS analysis, how does enlarging the polymer backbone from IDT to IDTT affect the (001) diffraction peak and d-spacing?
qa_pairs.answer: Enlarging the backbone shifts the (001) diffraction peak to a lower value and increases the d-spacing. Specifically, the IDT-based polymers (PhIDT-TQxT and ThIDT-TQxT) show a peak at 0.56 Å⁻¹ with a d-spacing of 11.2 Å, whereas the backbone-enlarged PhIDTT-TQxT exhibits a peak at 0.48 Å⁻¹ with a larger d-spacing of 13.1 Å.
qa_pairs.source_title: Enhancement of the Power-Conversion Efficiency of Organic Solar Cells via Unveiling an Appropriate Rational Design Strategy in Indacenodithiophene-alt-quinoxaline π-Conjugated Polymers

qa_pairs.question: Which of the studied IDT-quinoxaline polymers exhibits the highest molar extinction coefficient, and what is its value?
qa_pairs.answer: ThIDT-TQxT exhibits the highest molar extinction coefficient (ε) among the studied polymers, with a value of 60,560 cm⁻¹ L mol⁻¹ at 570 nm in chloroform, outperforming both PhIDTT-TQxT (48,780) and PhIDT-TQxT(LMW) (44,250).
qa_pairs.source_title: Enhancement of the Power-Conversion Efficiency of Organic Solar Cells via Unveiling an Appropriate Rational Design Strategy in Indacenodithiophene-alt-quinoxaline π-Conjugated Polymers

qa_pairs.question: What role does the solvent additive 1-chloronaphthalene (CN) play in the morphology and performance of IDT-quinoxaline polymer:PC71BM blend films?
qa_pairs.answer: The addition of 1-chloronaphthalene (CN) reduces nanophase separation and significantly decreases the surface roughness of the blend films from 2.2-13.9 nm down to 0.5-0.6 nm. This morphological improvement leads to a significant enhancement in the power conversion efficiency (PCE).
qa_pairs.source_title: Enhancement of the Power-Conversion Efficiency of Organic Solar Cells via Unveiling an Appropriate Rational Design Strategy in Indacenodithiophene-alt-quinoxaline π-Conjugated Polymers

qa_pairs.question: Compare the electron-hole transfer rates of ThIDT-TQxT and PhIDT-TQxT(LMW) as determined by transient absorption spectroscopy (TAS).
qa_pairs.answer: ThIDT-TQxT, which features thienyl substitution, exhibits a faster electron-hole transfer process with a time component (τ2) of 17 ps. In contrast, the phenyl-substituted PhIDT-TQxT(LMW) has a slower transfer rate with a τ2 of 25 ps.
qa_pairs.source_title: Enhancement of the Power-Conversion Efficiency of Organic Solar Cells via Unveiling an Appropriate Rational Design Strategy in Indacenodithiophene-alt-quinoxaline π-Conjugated Polymers

qa_pairs.question: How does increasing the molecular weight or enlarging the polymer backbone to IDTT influence the charge transfer kinetics in these materials?
qa_pairs.answer: Both increasing the molecular weight (HMW) and enlarging the polymer backbone (IDTT) lead to slower electron-hole transfer rates. PhIDT-TQxT(HMW) and PhIDTT-TQxT exhibit τ2 time components of 33 ps and 46 ps, respectively, which are considerably slower than their lower molecular weight or standard IDT backbone counterparts, thereby suppressing electrical performance.
qa_pairs.source_title: Enhancement of the Power-Conversion Efficiency of Organic Solar Cells via Unveiling an Appropriate Rational Design Strategy in Indacenodithiophene-alt-quinoxaline π-Conjugated Polymers
